title: Add RAG playback simulator + deterministic testing harness with CLI and CI workflow
author: Priya Singh
description: Motivation: teams building RAG integrations need a deterministic, reviewable way to validate end-to-end behavior (retrieval, tool-calls, and model responses) across local dev and CI. This PR introduces a small, opinionated playback simulator and test harness that records a reference interaction trace and replays it with deterministic seeding and snapshot assertions so we can detect regressions in prompt wiring, routing, or SDK changes. Key features included: a lightweight CLI (playback run, record, snapshot-update), a JSONL trace format for portability, a fixtures directory with example queries and a small sample index, a Pytest integration that can be run locally and on CI, a GitHub Actions workflow template for nightly replay runs, and docs/quickstart content that explains how to adopt the harness. Security note: recorded traces redact sensitive fields by default; instructions included for additional redaction. Migration: no breaking API changes to SDKs; this is an examples-only addition that teams can opt into. Testing checklist: [x] manual record/playback of 10 canonical queries, [x] automated test run in CI with deterministic random seed, [x] docs quickstart and code sample reviewed, [x] small Dockerfile for CI containerization. How to run: examples/rag-playback/README.md shows 'playback record --out examples/rag-playback/fixtures/sample.trace.jsonl' and 'playback run --trace fixtures/sample.trace.jsonl --ci-mode --assert-snapshots'. CI integration: .github/workflows/rag-playback-ci.yml runs python -m pytest examples/rag-playback/tests and uploads trace artifacts on failure. Long-term: this harness will be used by the QA and SDK teams to create a regression suite for routing and structured output changes. Related: ENG-2311 (playback harness), ENG-2409 (CI guardrails), SUP-8421 (customer-reported flaky RAG behavior).
